text:
Ottawa arrives off a 7-4 win over the Rangers, in which Drake Batherson scored three goals, and sits 3-2-0 in its last five, though it is playing without Thomas Chabot and William Eklund. Tyler Kleven has moved in beside Jake Sanderson's partner Spence on defense, and Warren Foegele and Stephen Halliday have picked up Eklund's minutes. Vegas is winless in three (0-2-1) after a 2-1 overtime loss at Columbus, though the chances say that is mostly bad luck: the Golden Knights got 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in those games, and Mitch Marner could return.

At five on five, OTT has taken 51% of the expected goals and VGK 54%, so there isn't much between them. Vegas has the cleaner penalty kill, allowing 0.34 expected goals a game to Ottawa's 0.68, and Ottawa takes 4.9 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side power plays. Both projected goalies are below par: Jonas Johansson (OTT) is at -0.1 goals saved above expected this season and -10.7 last season, while Adin Hill (VGK) is at -2.4 and -15.0.

Tim Stützle has goals in three straight and a 33% chance to score; Batherson sits at 31%. For Vegas, Mark Stone, who was drafted by the Senators in 2010, is our top goal pick at 34%, and Jack Eichel is at 30%, with the Vegas Hockey Knight writing of a noticeable change in his game this season. Our model has this nearly even: 3.04 expected goals for VGK, 2.95 for OTT.
